examples.en: On rainy days I think of pajeon.
I dip pajeon in spicy soy sauce.
On the weekend my mom pan-fried pajeon for me.
Excuse me, one seafood pajeon, please.

examples.ko: 프라이팬 위에서 파전이 노릇노릇 익고 있어요.
examples.en: The pajeon is cooking golden brown in the frying pan.

examples.ko: 파전 반죽에 오징어를 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you put squid in the pajeon batter.

explain: '부침개'는 기름에 부친 음식 전체이고, 파전은 그중 파가 들어간 것이에요. 동사는 '부치다'를 써서 '파전을 부치다'라고 해요. '붙이다'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 한국 사람들은 비 오는 날 기름 소리가 빗소리 같아서 파전을 먹는다고 말해요.

phrases.en: On rainy days we eat pan-fried pancakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름에 부친 음식 전체를 부르는 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for all kinds of pan-fried pancakes.

phrases.en: My mother made pajeon for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파전을 만들 때는 '부치다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'buchida' when making pajeon.

phrases.en: One pajeon, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파전은 '한 장'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pajeon is counted with 'one jang'.

explain_en: 'Buchimgae' is the general word for pan-fried batter dishes, and pajeon is the kind with green onions. The verb is '부치다' (pan-fry), as in '파전을 부치다', not '붙이다' (stick). Koreans often say they crave pajeon on rainy days because the sizzling sounds like rain.

examples.en: They say I'm curious because I'm a Monkey in the zodiac.
My older sister is a Monkey and I am a Dog.
I met a friend who was born in a Monkey year.
Are you a Monkey too, teacher? That's the same as me.

examples.ko: 원숭이띠 해는 열두 해마다 다시 돌아와요.
examples.en: A Monkey year comes around again every twelve years.

examples.ko: 올해 원숭이띠가 운이 좋다고 해서 기대돼요.
examples.en: They say Monkeys have good luck this year, so I'm looking forward to it.

explain: 십이지 동물로 태어난 해를 말해요. '무슨 띠예요?'에 '원숭이띠예요'라고 대답해요. '신년 운세'에서 띠별로 운을 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: 2016 was the Year of the Monkey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 원숭이에 해당하는 해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the year itself, not the person born in it.

phrases.en: I read the Monkey sign's fortune in the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띠별 운세를 읽을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when reading zodiac fortunes.

phrases.en: I'm a Monkey. My friend is an Ox.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무슨 띠예요?'에 대답하는 가장 쉬운 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest answer to 무슨 띠예요?

explain_en: It names the zodiac animal of the year you were born. You answer '무슨 띠예요?' with '원숭이띠예요'. Zodiac signs are often used in New Year fortune readings.

examples.en: Tomorrow is my grandfather's memorial day, so I'm going to my uncle's house.
On memorial day the family gathers to prepare food.

examples.ko: 제삿날이 다가오면 어머니가 장을 많이 보세요.
examples.en: When the memorial day approaches, my mother does a lot of grocery shopping.
It's a relief that this year's memorial day falls on the weekend.

examples.ko: 제삿날 아침부터 집에서 전 부치는 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: From the morning of the memorial day, the house smelled of pan-fried jeon.
I told the office it was a memorial day and left early.

explain: '제사'는 지내는 일이고 '제삿날'은 그 날짜예요. 같은 날을 '기일'이라고도 하는데, 일상 대화에서는 '제삿날이 다음 주예요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Next week is my grandmother's memorial day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제삿날'과 같은 날인데, 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the same day, but a slightly more formal word.

phrases.example: 제삿날에는 온 가족이 모여 제사를 지내요.
phrases.en: On the memorial day, the whole family gathers and holds the ritual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제사를 하는 일을 말할 때 '지내다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '지내다' is the verb used for holding the ritual.

phrases.en: The memorial day was coming up, so my mother went grocery shopping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날짜가 가까워질 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the date is getting close.

explain_en: '제사' is the ritual itself and '제삿날' is the date it is held. The same day is also called '기일', but in everyday talk people often say things like '제삿날이 다음 주예요'.

examples.ko: 투표일이 공휴일이라서 여행 가는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Voting day is a holiday, so some people go on trips.

examples.ko: 투표일 전에 후보들의 공약을 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: Before voting day, I checked the candidates' pledges.
When is voting day for this election?

examples.ko: 투표일에 일이 있으면 미리 사전 투표를 하세요.
examples.en: If you have something on voting day, vote early in advance.
There aren't many days left until voting day.
I marked voting day on the calendar so I wouldn't forget.

explain: '선거일'과 거의 같은 날을 가리키지만, '사전 투표일'처럼 미리 투표하는 날을 따로 말할 때도 써요. '투표일'은 투표하는 날, '선거일'은 선거가 있는 날이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: On voting day I went to the polling place with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 투표하는 날이 언제인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '에' says when the voting day is.

phrases.example: 사전 투표일은 선거 날보다 며칠 먼저예요.
phrases.en: Early voting day is a few days before election day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 투표하는 날을 따로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer separately to the days for early voting.

phrases.en: On election day, many schools are closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투표일과 거의 같은 날이지만 선거가 있는 날이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually the same day, but it feels like 'the day of the election.'

explain_en: It points to nearly the same day as '선거일', but it is also used for separate voting days such as '사전 투표일' (early voting day). '투표일' feels like the day you vote, and '선거일' like the day the election takes place.

examples.en: I memorize Korean words whenever I have a spare moment.
I know you're busy, but come visit when you get a chance.

examples.ko: 요즘은 틈날 때마다 공원에서 산책을 해요.
examples.en: These days I take a walk in the park whenever I have time.
I found a free moment at lunchtime and took a short nap.
Rest even briefly when you get a free moment.
After the meeting ends, I'll call you as soon as I get a free moment.

explain: '시간이 나다'와 비슷하지만, 바쁜 중에 잠깐 생긴 짧은 시간이라는 느낌이 강해요. '틈나는 대로', '틈날 때마다'처럼 자주 쓰고, '틈이 나다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I read books whenever I have a spare moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 생길 때마다 바로 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means doing something as soon as you get free time.

phrases.en: I call my parents whenever I have a free moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '틈나는 대로'와 비슷하고 반복해서 한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 틈나는 대로, with a feeling of doing it again and again.
phrases.en_equiv: every time I get a chance

phrases.en: If I find some time today, I plan to take a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '틈나다'와 같은 뜻이고, '이'를 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 틈나다, with '이' added.

explain_en: It is similar to '시간이 나다' but strongly suggests a short gap in an otherwise busy schedule. It is common in '틈나는 대로' and '틈날 때마다', and you can also say '틈이 나다'.

en: to be planned; to be scheduled

examples.en: This trip was planned a very long time ago.
The park construction is planned for next year.
We set off according to the planned schedule.

examples.ko: 모임이 계획되면 단체 채팅방에 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: When a get-together is planned, I'll tell you in the group chat.

examples.ko: 새 지하철역이 이 지역에 계획되고 있어요.
examples.en: A new subway station is being planned for this area.
The event that was first planned was suddenly canceled.

explain: '계획하다'는 사람이 세우는 것이고, '계획되다'는 어떤 일이 이미 계획 안에 들어 있는 상태예요. 공사·행사·일정처럼 큰 일에 잘 쓰고, 개인 이야기는 '계획이 있어요'나 '계획을 세웠어요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 새 도서관 공사가 계획돼 있어요.
phrases.en: A new library construction is planned for next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 이미 계획에 들어 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 있다' describes something already in the plan.

phrases.en: The planned event was canceled because of rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '미리 계획한 일'을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun to mean something that was planned in advance.

phrases.en: No trip is planned for this summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 계획에 없다는 것을 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not yet in the plan.

explain_en: Passive; an event or trip is arranged in advance. '계획하다' is a person making a plan; '계획되다' is something already being in the plan. It suits bigger things like construction, events and schedules. For personal talk, '계획이 있어요' or '계획을 세웠어요' sounds more natural.

dis.h: general word for being planned out
gh: designed as an organized project or event
set for a certain time; scheduled

p.n: 기획 sounds like an organized project designed by a team.

t90.ax: This trip was planned a very long time ago.

examples.en: Four or five friends came over to hang out.
I bought four or five apples at the market.
We meet around four or five o'clock.
The kids look to be about four or five years old.

examples.ko: 집이 멀어서 버스를 네다섯 번 갈아탔어요.
examples.en: My home is far, so I changed buses four or five times.

examples.ko: 저는 한 달에 책을 네다섯 권 읽어요.
examples.en: I read about four or five books a month.

explain: 정확한 숫자를 모를 때 어림잡아 말해요. 뒤에 '명, 개, 시, 살, 권'처럼 세는 말이 와요. '네댓'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고 말할 때는 이쪽도 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I bought four or five apples at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 말할 때 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and often heard in speech.

phrases.en: There are four or five students in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수를 어림잡아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give a rough number of people.

phrases.en: I watched that movie four or five times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 횟수를 대충 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give a rough number of times.

explain_en: Four or five — standard everyday form, used in all speech. You use it to give an approximate number when you don't know the exact one. A counter such as 명, 개, 시, 살 or 권 follows it. '네댓' has the same meaning and is also heard often in speech.

t90.ax: We meet around four or five o'clock.

en: to treat (a guest) to food or drink; to entertain

examples.en: I serve food to guests who come to my home.
Yesterday I treated my teacher to lunch.
Today I will treat you to a delicious dinner.
There is a culture of treating guests warmly.

examples.ko: 부모님을 대접하고 싶어서 좋은 식당을 예약했어요.
examples.en: I booked a nice restaurant because I wanted to treat my parents.

examples.ko: 대접받은 만큼 저도 잘 대접하려고 해요.
examples.en: I also try to treat others well in return for how I was treated.

explain: 손님이나 윗사람에게 음식을 차려 주거나 사 줄 때 써요. 받는 쪽은 '대접받다'이고, 안 좋게 대하는 것은 '푸대접'이에요. 윗사람에게는 '대접해 드리다'로 높여요.

phrases.en: I treated my parents to dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 대접할 때 높여서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for treating someone older or senior.

phrases.en: I was treated to delicious food at my friend's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대접을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being treated.

phrases.en: I treated them to a meal to show thanks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '대접'을 써서 음식을 사 주는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 대접 for the act of treating someone to a meal.

explain_en: Entertain — serve a guest food or drink, showing hospitality. Use it when you serve or buy food for guests or elders. The receiving side is '대접받다', and poor treatment is '푸대접'. For elders, make it polite with '대접해 드리다'.

t90.ax: Yesterday I treated my teacher to lunch.

examples.en: I made a new friend who is the same age as me.
Since we were all the same age, we talked comfortably.
That actor is the same age as me.
I went on a trip to Jeju with friends my age.
We are the same age, so we became close quickly.
Meeting someone my age abroad makes me really happy.

explain: '동갑'과 같은 뜻으로, 친근하게 부를 때 '동갑내기'라고 해요. '-내기'는 '시골내기', '신출내기'처럼 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요. 한국에서는 나이로 말투를 정하는 일이 있어서 동갑인지 먼저 묻기도 해요.

phrases.en: We are the same age.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동갑내기'와 같은 뜻이고, 더 짧고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '동갑내기', but shorter and more common.

phrases.en: We're friends the same age, so we talk casually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 같은 친구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a friend who is the same age.

phrases.en: We are the same age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자말 없이 풀어서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, easy way to say it without the Sino-Korean word.

explain_en: It means the same as '동갑' but sounds friendlier. The ending '-내기' attaches to people, as in '시골내기' and '신출내기'. In Korea speech style can depend on age, so people sometimes ask first whether you are 동갑.

examples.en: In winter you stay warm if you sleep under a cotton comforter.

examples.ko: 할머니 집에 가면 두꺼운 솜이불이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a thick cotton comforter at Grandma's house.
Cotton comforters are hard to wash, so we air them in the sun.
I fell asleep right away after lying under the cotton comforter.
I crawled under the cotton comforter to warm up.
I wrapped the baby snugly in a cotton comforter.

explain: 안에 솜을 넣어 만든 이불이에요. 이불은 '덮다', 바닥에 까는 것은 '요'라고 해서 '요를 깔고 이불을 덮다'라고 말해요. 요즘은 솜 대신 오리털이나 극세사로 만든 이불도 많아요.

phrases.en: It got cold, so I took the cotton comforter out of the closet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울이 되어 이불을 준비할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting bedding ready for winter.
phrases.en_equiv: to take out a cotton comforter

phrases.en: The weather was nice, so I dried the cotton comforter in the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 솜이불은 햇볕에 말리는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cotton comforters are often dried in the sun.

phrases.en: The cotton comforter is heavy, so it's hard to wash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 솜이불의 무게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the comforter's weight.

explain_en: It is a comforter filled with cotton batting. You 'cover yourself' with an 이불, while the one laid on the floor is a '요', so people say '요를 깔고 이불을 덮다'. Nowadays many comforters are made with down or microfiber instead of cotton.

examples.ko: 부모님이 딸을 시집보내고 나서 많이 우셨어요.
examples.en: My parents cried a lot after marrying off their daughter.
My father felt empty after marrying off his youngest daughter.
They say in the old days, daughters were married off at around eighteen.
The house became quiet after my older sister was married off.

examples.ko: 딸을 시집보내려고 몇 년 동안 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: I saved money for years to marry off my daughter.
I have no plans yet to marry off my daughter.

explain: 딸이 결혼해서 남편 집으로 가는 것을 부모의 입장에서 말할 때 써요. 아들이 결혼하는 경우에는 '장가보내다'를 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '시집가다'와 '시집오다'예요.

phrases.en: After marrying off my daughter, the house became quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딸이 결혼한 후의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what happens after a daughter marries.

phrases.en: I got my son married last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딸은 '시집보내다', 아들은 '장가보내다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 시집보내다 for a daughter and 장가보내다 for a son.

phrases.en: My older sister is getting married next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신부 본인의 입장에서 말하는 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The matching word from the bride's own point of view.

explain_en: It describes a daughter marrying and going to her husband's family, from the parents' point of view. For a son marrying, use '장가보내다'. Related words are '시집가다' and '시집오다'.

t90.ax: I have no plans yet to marry off my daughter.

examples.en: Ugh, I'm so tired again today.
Oh dear, it's raining again.
Phew, I got such a fright.
Phew, it's finally over.
Ugh! Why is the room so hot?
Oh, please stop it already.

explain: 힘들 때, 안심할 때, 어이없을 때 모두 나오는 소리라서 표정과 억양으로 느낌이 달라져요. 비슷한 소리로 '아이고'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Oh dear, I'm late again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아휴'와 비슷하게 힘들거나 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 아휴, used when tired or surprised.

phrases.en: Phew, what a relief. I passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 끝나고 안심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a worry is over and you feel relieved.

phrases.en: Ugh, I'm tired. I want to rest a bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 마음이 힘들 때 한숨처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like a sigh when you are worn out.

explain_en: It comes out when you are tired, relieved, or exasperated, so the feeling depends on your face and intonation. A similar sound is 아이고.
